MUSC 100.title: Principles of Musical Form
MUSC 100.description: Explain rhythmic, melodic, textural, and harmonic materials and processes of music, and how they create small-scale structures. Fluency with music notation advised. B.Mus. and B.A. Music students with a strong background in music theory may test into MUSC_V 101.

MUSC 101.title: Diatonic Harmony and Voice Leading
MUSC 101.description: Harmonic and linear functions of diatonic chords; common progressions and sequences; introduction to tonal hierarchy and prolongation; simple modulation. Compositional and analytical exercises.

MUSC 103.title: Introduction to the Theory of Music
MUSC 103.description: Concepts of rhythm, pitch, timbre, and texture. Notation and aural recognition of rhythmic and pitch patterns. Basic principles of melody and form. Background in Western music theory or notation unnecessary. This course is inapplicable to the B.Mus. or B.A. Music.

MUSC 104.title: Introduction to Diatonic Harmony
MUSC 104.description: Triads, key and elementary harmony in Western music. Elements of musical form. Aural training and exercises in composition, modeled on historical styles. Not for credit in the B.Mus.

MUSC 105.title: Aural Skills I
MUSC 105.description: Sight singing; melodic and harmonic dictation; rhythm production; error detection; tuning; perception of harmony, form, and tonality; improvisation in set idioms. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

MUSC 106.title: Aural Skills II
MUSC 106.description: Continuation of MUSC_V 105. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

MUSC 108.title: Introduction to Contemporary Art Music
MUSC 108.description: Contemporary music repertoire, emphasizing music from the past fifty years. Required of undergraduate Composition majors; open to other Bachelor of Music students by permission of instructor.

MUSC 112.title: Class Brasses and Percussion
MUSC 112.description: Group instruction in music performance. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

MUSC 119.title: Introduction to Music Technology
MUSC 119.description: Practical and theoretical training in technologies that support current artistic and academic practice, such as MIDI, podcasts/videocasts, websites, social media, and software for score notation, music education, and basic audio/video editing.

MUSC 120.title: History of Music I
MUSC 120.description: An overview of Western music from antiquity through the Middle Ages and Renaissance, providing a framework for understanding musical styles and practices, and examining selected compositions in greater analytical and historical depth.

MUSC 121.title: History of Music II
MUSC 121.description: The development of Western music from circa 1600 to circa 1800.
MUSC 121.prerequisiteText: MUSC 120. Or permission of the instructor

MUSC 122.title: Class Woodwinds
MUSC 122.description: Group instruction in music performance. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

MUSC 128.title: Music and Human Experience
MUSC 128.description: A multi-disciplinary survey of music in selected world traditions and genres, connecting it to ideas of time, evolution, history, anthropology, philosophy, and contemporary globalised culture.

MUSC 131.title: Class Voice
MUSC 131.description: Group instruction in music performance. Required of all first-time secondary voice students. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

MUSC 135.title: Opera Repertoire I
MUSC 135.description: A musico-dramatic study and analysis of representative works in the international operatic theatre from 1600 to the present, through musical, literary and graphic sources. Each sequential year of study, the student is expected to show increased facility in musical and dramatic analysis as well as a greater understanding of the works under examination. Open to students outside the B.Mus. program by permission of the instructor.

MUSC 136.title: Piano Repertoire I
MUSC 136.description: Performance and discussion of the repertoire for string-keyboard instruments essential to the performer and teacher. Special attention to matters of structure, style, and performance practices. Required of piano performance majors and open to piano concentrators, space permitting. First term prerequisite to second term.

MUSC 141.title: Class Piano I
MUSC 141.description: Required of all first-time secondary piano students.

MUSC 149.title: Collaborative Piano I
MUSC 149.description: Skills and performance practice with primary emphasis on voice/piano partnership principles and repertoire. Strong sight-reading skills essential. For Piano majors; open to others by audition.

MUSC 150.title: Large Instrumental Ensemble (Lower Years)
MUSC 150.description: Symphony Orchestra, Symphonic Wind Ensemble, or Concert Winds. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 151.title: University Chamber Orchestra (Lower Years)
MUSC 151.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 153.title: University Singers (Lower Years)
MUSC 153.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 154.title: University Choral Union (Lower Years)
MUSC 154.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 156.title: Vocal Chamber Ensembles (Lower Years)
MUSC 156.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 157.title: Early Music Ensemble (Lower Years)
MUSC 157.description: Performance of early Western instrumental and vocal ensemble music. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 159.title: University Chamber Strings (Lower Years)
MUSC 159.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 160.title: String Chamber Ensembles (Lower Years)
MUSC 160.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 161.title: Piano Chamber Ensembles (Lower Years)
MUSC 161.description: Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 162.title: Wind and Percussion Chamber Ensembles (Lower Years)
MUSC 162.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

MUSC 163.title: Contemporary Players (Lower Years)
MUSC 163.description: Performance of contemporary music. An ensemble of variable size, including both instrumentalists and singers, will be formed to present several concerts of 20th-century music during the academic year. May be taken twice for credit.

MUSC 164.title: Jazz Ensemble (Lower Years)
MUSC 164.description: Performance techniques and repertoire. May be taken twice for credit.

MUSC 165.title: World Music Ensembles (Lower Years)
MUSC 165.description: Training on traditional instruments and their techniques, with emphasis on ensemble performance. Different sections focus on the music of different cultures, e.g., Bali, China, Ghana, Korea. May be taken twice for credit.

MUSC 167.title: Introduction to Piano Chamber Music
MUSC 167.description: A survey of repertoire and performance issues.

MUSC 169.title: Intensive Chamber Ensemble (Lower Years)
MUSC 169.description: Intensive coaching in chamber ensemble for advanced players. Performance of works prepared is expected. May be taken twice for credit.
MUSC 169.corequisiteText: Any small ensemble (MUSC 156-166) and permission of the instructor

MUSC 170.title: Lyric Diction
MUSC 170.description: A study of the basic phonetics and accepted principles of lyric diction of the four languages most commonly used in concert and operatic repertoire: French, German, Italian, and English.

MUSC 200.title: Chromatic Harmony and Voice Leading
MUSC 200.description: Harmonic and linear functions of common chromatic chords; mixture; chords and progressions of linear origin; tonal plans. Compositional and analytical exercises.

MUSC 201.title: Musical Forms
MUSC 201.description: Study of various forms in tonal music and the rhythmic, melodic, textural, and harmonic processes that create them on small and large scales. Compositional and analytical exercises.

MUSC 205.title: Aural Skills III
MUSC 205.description: Continuation of MUSC_V 106. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

MUSC 221.title: History of Music IV
MUSC 221.description: The development of Western music from circa 1900; an introduction to jazz and popular music and to music of selected non-Western societies.

MUSC 249.title: Collaborative Piano II
MUSC 249.description: Further development of skills and performance practice with primary emphasis on voice/piano partnership principles and repertoire. Strong sight-reading skills essential. For Piano majors; open to others by audition.

MUSC 300.title: Compositional and Analytical Approaches to Post-Tonal Music
MUSC 300.description: Concepts essential to understanding and performing art music, since 1900, in which functional triadic harmony is absent or subsidiary to other musical processes. Detailed consideration of works of major composers up to the present, through analysis, composition, and musicianship exercises.

MUSC 305.title: Readings in Orchestral Repertoire
MUSC 305.description: Laboratory course for orchestral performance majors. Emphasis on reading a large cross-section of standard orchestral repertoire, especially music currently being programmed by local professional orchestras. Restricted to Orchestral Instruments majors, except by permission of the instructor.

MUSC 307.title: Composition III

MUSC 309.title: Instrumentation
MUSC 309.description: The study of string, woodwind, brass and percussion instruments; orchestral sections and scoring for various small ensembles. Activities include demonstrations of instruments, scoring projects, analysis and listening. For credit towards the B.Mus. and the B.A. in Music; not open to other students.

children.raw: completion of the second-year piano requirement

MUSC 309.prerequisiteText: MUSC 200. and completion of the second-year piano requirement

MUSC 310.title: Orchestration
MUSC 310.description: The study of orchestration through the analysis of orchestral works, listening and scoring projects. Activities also include choral arranging and scoring for stage band and wind ensemble.

MUSC 311.title: Fundamentals of Conducting
MUSC 311.description: Basic conducting techniques: patterns, cueing, dynamic shading, and physical presentation.

children.raw: completion of the second-year piano requirement

MUSC 311.prerequisiteText: MUSC_V 200 and completion of the second-year piano requirement

MUSC 312.title: Instrumental Conducting
MUSC 312.description: The relation of conducting gestures to instrumental sound; development of practical skills in directing ensembles and reading scores, considering instruments' special characteristics.

MUSC 313.title: Choral Conducting
MUSC 313.description: The relation of conducting gestures to choral sound; development of practical skills in directing ensembles and reading scores; attendant issues of vocal technique and pedagogy.

MUSC 319.title: Electroacoustic Music
MUSC 319.description: Study of acoustics, audio technology, and electroacoustic composition. Composition of original works using the UBC Electroacoustic Music Studio or students' own software/hardware.

children.raw: Permission of instructor is also required

MUSC 319.prerequisiteText: MUSC 119 and one of MUSC 100, MUSC 103. Permission of instructor is also required

MUSC 320.title: Computer Music
MUSC 320.description: The study of computer applications to music, focusing on digital synthesis techniques and languages, methods of algorithmic composition, and the design of music editors.

MUSC 321.title: Music Appreciation, Twentieth-Century
MUSC 321.description: Designed for students with little or no musical background. Not for credit toward the B.Mus. or B.A. in Music.

MUSC 322.title: Topics in Western Music
MUSC 322.description: Study in one major genre of Western music (e.g., The Symphony, Women in Opera, History of the Song Cycle). No musical knowledge is required. Not for credit toward the B.Mus. or B.A. in Music.

MUSC 323.title: History of Popular Music
MUSC 323.description: Genres of popular music from 1950 to the present and their changing aesthetic, social, cultural, and historical dimensions. Prior experience with music notation and terminology is not required. This course is not acceptable for credit toward the B.Mus., or toward the B.A. major, honours, or minor in Music.

MUSC 324.title: The Guitar in History and Practice
MUSC 324.description: Introduction to guitar performance and repertoire for non-majors. Lectures explore guitar repertoires from selected regions and eras. Not for credit toward the B.Mus. or the Major/Minor in Music (B.A., B.F.A., B.Sc.). Students are expected to provide their own guitars.

MUSC 326.title: Music Appreciation
MUSC 326.description: An introductory course for which previous musical background is helpful, but not required. Contents include a discussion of musical concepts, evolution of forms, style, and media and detailed study of selected works from the concert repertoire. Popular forms of music (jazz, folk, rock, etc) not included. Not for credit towards the B.Mus. or B.A. in Music.

MUSC 327.title: Cantonese Music
MUSC 327.description: A history of musical genres with Cantonese lyrics from the nineteenth century to the present. Topics include music and text relationships, major singers, major genres (narrative songs, Cantonese opera, Cantopop).

MUSC 328.title: World Music Cultures
MUSC 328.description: Introduction to the principles of ethnomusicology and an examination of at least two contrasting musical traditions. May be repeated once for credit if different traditions are covered.

MUSC 330.title: Music in Vancouver's Ethnic Communities
MUSC 330.description: Examination of music within the ethnic context as found in the urban environment of Vancouver. The musics of several traditions (e.g., Chinese, Jewish, English folk) will be studied together with the social issues surrounding their preservation. For credit toward the B.Mus. and the B.A. in Music, but open to students not majoring in music.

MUSC 331.title: Workshop in World Rhythm
MUSC 331.description: Theory and practice of selected rhythmic systems of world music cultures, focusing on West African drumming, and including other systems such as Indian Tala and Peking opera percussion.

MUSC 333.title: Accompanying on the Harpsichord I
MUSC 333.description: Basic techniques and styles of continuo playing. Open to keyboard players with no previous harpsichord experience.

MUSC 336.title: Opera Theatre Techniques I
MUSC 336.description: Performance techniques associated with the musical theatre of various historical periods. Basic dance. Most operatic excerpts will be in English.

MUSC 339.title: Opera Workshop I
MUSC 339.description: Participation in performances by the School. Open also to students outside Music without credit, after audition.

MUSC 340.title: Piano Pedagogy I: Theory and Studio Management
MUSC 340.description: Basic principles of teaching piano. Business aspects of establishing and maintaining a music studio. For Piano Performance majors; open to other Bachelor of Music students by permission of the instructor.

MUSC 345.title: Aesthetics and Practice of Film Music

MUSC 349.title: Keyboard Harmony and Transposition
MUSC 349.description: Designed for the keyboard performance major and keyboard concentrator in General Studies.

MUSC 350.title: Large Instrumental Ensemble (Upper Years)
MUSC 350.description: Symphony Orchestra, Symphonic Wind Ensemble, or Concert Winds. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 351.title: University Chamber Orchestra (Upper Years)
MUSC 351.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 352.title: History of Medieval Music
MUSC 352.description: Sacred and secular music, vocal and instrumental.

MUSC 353.title: History of Renaissance Music
MUSC 353.description: Sacred and secular music, vocal and instrumental.

MUSC 358.title: History of Jazz
MUSC 358.description: Jazz styles and their cultural contexts; the relationship of performers and audiences; issues of race and gender; non-Western influences.

MUSC 359.title: University Chamber Strings (Upper Years)
MUSC 359.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 360.title: String Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
MUSC 360.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 361.title: Piano Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
MUSC 361.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to other students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 362.title: Wind and Percussion Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
MUSC 362.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 363.title: History and Repertoire of the Guitar and Related Instruments
MUSC 363.description: A chronological survey, from the Renaissance to the present day, of music for the guitar and related instruments and of the development of the instruments themselves. Instruments considered include Renaissance and Baroque lutes, the vihuela, and early types of guitar as well as the modern six-string guitar. Musical forms and genres, national schools and the works of principal composers of every period are explored and attention is given to national systems, continuo realization, historical ornamentation and pedagogical systems.

MUSC 365.title: Song Repertoire I
MUSC 365.description: An exploration of the solo art song repertoire from 1600 to the Romantic period. Repertoire essential to the performer and teacher will be studied through live and recorded performance with special attention given to poetic content and musical style.

MUSC 366.title: University Choral Union (Upper Years)
MUSC 366.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 369.title: Intensive Chamber Ensemble (Upper Years)
MUSC 369.description: Intensive coaching in chamber ensemble for advanced players. Performance of works prepared is expected. May be taken twice for credit. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.
MUSC 369.corequisiteText: One of MUSC 350, MUSC 351, MUSC 359, MUSC 360, MUSC 361, MUSC 362, MUSC 366, MUSC 453, MUSC 456, MUSC 457, MUSC 463, MUSC 466. and permission of the instructor

MUSC 394.prerequisiteText: One of MUSC_V 271, MUSC _V 272, MUSC_V 281, MUSC_V 283, MUSC_V 291, MUSC_V 292, MUSC_V 293

MUSC 402.title: Special Projects
MUSC 402.description: For fourth-year students who receive permission of the Director of the School of Music to do advanced studies in their major field.

MUSC 403.title: Selected Topics in Music
MUSC 403.description: See School of Music schedule for description and prerequisites. Restricted to B. Mus. and B.A. in Music students.

MUSC 409.title: Jazz Theory and Arranging
MUSC 409.description: Jazz scales, chord relationships, substitutions, orchestration, listening, and score analysis. Restricted to B.Mus. and B.A. in Music students.

MUSC 410.title: Introduction to Schenkerian Analysis
MUSC 410.description: The key concepts of Schenker's theory of tonality. Applications to the analysis of short pieces in various tonal styles, emphasizing clear and correct graphing. Issues of interpretive scope.

MUSC 411.title: Analysis of Tonal Music
MUSC 411.description: Analytical approaches that complement Schenkerian analysis, including motivic construction, harmonic rhythm and phrase rhythm, chromaticism and enharmonicism, features of musical form, aspects of structure and hierarchy at the small and large scale.

MUSC 412.title: Analytical Studies in the Development of Musical Modernism (1860 - 1940)
MUSC 412.description: Analysis of late- and post-romantic works within a theoretical framework that bridges earlier to later works. Assignments in various formats, emphasizing analysis but possibly including composition.

MUSC 413.title: Contemporary Art Music: Theory and Analysis
MUSC 413.description: A technical approach to the diverse concert-music repertoire since 1950, including orchestral, chamber, solo, and electro-acoustic genres. Applicable theories of pitch and rhythm, with reference to composers' own writings.

MUSC 414.title: Counterpoint
MUSC 414.description: Analysis and composition of pieces that rely on the control and development of imitative, polyphonic textures. Models to be taken from one or more European historical repertoires.

MUSC 415.title: Imagining Musical Performances
MUSC 415.description: How performance and analysis engage the musical imagination, as complementary activities; how analytical observations can stimulate performance, and vice versa. Selected topics, with special emphasis on temporal factors.

MUSC 417.title: Musical Scoring for Film
MUSC 417.description: Addresses the practical aspects of composing music for film through assignments of written scores.

MUSC 419.title: Interactive Performance Systems
MUSC 419.description: Collaborative projects developing new connections between sound and gestures in live concert performance or responsive environments using multiple digital technologies. May be repeated once for credit.

MUSC 420.title: Music Technology Capstone Project
MUSC 420.description: Supervised individual music technology project on an approved topic. Restricted to students in the Minor in Applied Music Technology
MUSC 420.prerequisiteText: MUSC 419. And permission of the Instructor

MUSC 428.title: Topics in World Music
MUSC 428.description: The history, theory, style, organology, and forms of the music of a particular culture in its aesthetic and cultural context. Students should consult the School as to which music culture will be covered in a particular year. May be repeated once for credit if different cultures are covered.

MUSC 430.title: Major Composers
MUSC 430.description: The musical works of no more than two significant composers will be examined. Specific topics will be announced; may be repeated for credit.
MUSC 430.prerequisiteText: All of MUSC 120, MUSC 121, MUSC 220, MUSC 221

MUSC 433.title: Accompanying on the Harpsichord II
MUSC 433.description: Continuation of MUSC_V 333 with emphasis on more advanced continuo and obbligato techniques.

MUSC 436.title: Opera Theatre Techniques II
MUSC 436.description: Advanced studies in acting, movement, gesture, dance and stage combat. Emphasis on communication and the art of singing and acting recitative in foreign languages.

MUSC 440.title: Piano Pedagogy II: Applications
MUSC 440.description: Teaching musical concepts and keyboard skills; observation of group and private lessons; supervised practicum. For Piano Performance majors; open to other Bachelor of Music students by permission of the instructor. Recommended pre-requisite: MUSC 340.

MUSC 441.title: Vocal Techniques
MUSC 441.description: A study of the scientific principles related to vocal performance: acoustical, physiological and psychological. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

MUSC 442.title: Song Interpretation
MUSC 442.description: Interpretation and performance practice of Art Song repertoire for voice and piano collaborations. Restricted to MMus and BMus in Piano Performance, Opera, Voice Performance, and students in the Diploma in Collaborative Piano Studies program.

MUSC 443.title: Opera Coaching
MUSC 443.description: Principles and practice, focusing on current Opera Workshop repertoire. Reproducing orchestrations on the piano; preparing scores; study of the voice and the rehearsal process; coaching languages; related conducting skills.

MUSC 444.title: Establishing a Career in Music
MUSC 444.description: Best practices of the contemporary business of music, focusing on understanding present market conditions, and on targeting specific opportunities through grant-writing, resums, press kits, publicity, recordings, and marketing. Restricted to fourth-year B.Mus. students.

MUSC 448.title: Historical Performance Practice
MUSC 448.description: Principles and practical application of the historically-informed performance of music. Philosophy, aesthetics, and key performance conventions of Western music before ca. 1800.
notes: Recommended: concurrent registration in MUSC 157 (Early Music Ensemble)

MUSC 450.title: Selected Topics in Vocal or Instrumental Genres
MUSC 450.description: Intensive study of one genre of music (e.g., orchestral music 17601849; the Lied in Austria and Germany) through analysis and the consideration of cultural milieu and historical development. Specific topics will be announced. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 credits.

MUSC 453.title: University Singers (Upper Years)
MUSC 453.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 454.title: History of Opera I
MUSC 454.description: The development of opera between 1600 and 1800.

MUSC 455.title: History of Opera II
MUSC 455.description: The development of opera between 1800 and the present.

MUSC 456.title: Vocal Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
MUSC 456.description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 457.title: Early Music Ensemble (Upper Years)
MUSC 457.description: Performance of early Western instrumental and vocal ensemble music. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 463.title: Contemporary Players (Upper Years)
MUSC 463.description: Performance of contemporary music. An ensemble of variable size, including both instrumentalists and singers, will be formed to present several concerts of 20th-century music during the academic year. May be taken twice for credit. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above.

MUSC 464.title: Jazz Ensemble (Upper Years)
